## Summary

"Life hack if your flight doesn't have Starlink: ask your agent to bypass the 443 split-TCP proxy via a $0.03/h BBR multiplexer and get ~4× faster, reset-free internet."

satmux targets the three things that actually break GEO-satellite cabin Wi-Fi (Inmarsat GX, Viasat, Panasonic, SITA) — none of which is raw bandwidth:

1. **Cabin `:443` middleboxes** — transparent split-TCP proxy (PEP) whose state table drops connections under load (TCP resets / TLS timeouts on GitHub, package registries); onboard DNS is intercepted too. Non-443 TCP ports pass untouched.
2. **Handshake tax** — every new origin pays multiple ~620 ms GEO round-trips (DNS + TCP + TLS) before first payload byte.
3. **Cubic congestion collapse** — cabin packet loss makes standard TCP halve cwnd repeatedly, leaving the per-seat token-bucket cap unused.

The fix: 12 pre-warmed persistent TCP carriers on `:8444` to a $0.01–0.03/h Linux ground VM near the satellite ground station (Amsterdam for Inmarsat GX / SITA AS206433 — i.e. Emirates & most EU/Middle East flights), with BBR + MSS 1280. Streams schedule onto the least-loaded carrier; SOCKS5/HTTP-CONNECT opens are 0-RTT (local OK in <1 ms); a ground-fetch mode does DNS + verified TLS 1.3 on fiber and zlib-compresses responses before they cross the satellite. Even wires `gh`/`git` through a local Unix socket so already-running coding agents keep working without restart. Measured 6-origin burst: 19.13 s (3/6 failed) → 5.35 s (0/6 failed), 3.6× faster, −76% TTFB (the tweet's photo shows a 6.4×/−78% run). Teardown after landing restores all proxy/git config with one command.

## Why it matters

- **Directly deployable on the user's airline.** Emirates / Middle East flights are the readme's first-listed case (Inmarsat GX via Amsterdam/Hetzner EU). Next long-haul without Starlink: rent VM, deploy, connect, benchmark — and the readme is written to be executed by a coding agent from one natural-language command ("spin up a temporary Ubuntu VM near my current satellite egress…").
- **The pattern generalizes:** middlebox bypass by port avoidance + moving TLS termination to fiber + compressing the expensive link. Same problem class as [[2026-10-01-cathrynlavery-tailscale]] (hostile networks), opposite objective — raw performance vs private geo-stable egress.
- **Agent-as-infrastructure:** the "ask your agent" framing is the real signal — this is a task only an agent reasonably executes mid-flight (VM provisioning, deploy, proxy wiring, teardown). One more datapoint that the agent's job description now includes "fix my plane's internet".
- **Skepticism gates:** single author, self-benchmarked on one provider (Inmarsat GX); burst numbers differ between his own two runs (3.6× readme vs 6.4× photo); incompressible media stays bounded by the ~4–5 Mbps per-seat shaper (zlib only helps HTML/JSON/code); custom PSK crypto (BLAKE2b+HMAC frames) is unaudited — fine for a perf tool, not for hostile-traffic protection; day-old repo. Doesn't bypass captive portals — needs your paid session. Speed-of-light floor (~600 ms RTT) doesn't move; he removes round-trips, not physics.
